segments.subgoal: Explain why Unity scripting support is needed and how to set up and create a C# script that customizes game-object behavior.
Describe the basic anatomy of a Unity C# script and how to inspect variable values and console output.
Explain how Unity scripts use built-in functions such as Destroy, user-defined functions, and event functions to control behavior and respond to gameplay events.
Describe how to instantiate prefabs at runtime by creating a script, attaching it to a game object, and referencing a prefab.
Describe the conditional and loop constructs supported in Unity C# scripts, including for, while, do-while, and foreach loops.
Explain how the Transform property stores and manipulates a game object’s position, rotation, and scale.
Explain how coroutines spread tasks across multiple frames, why they are not threads, and how they make effects such as fading visible.
Describe how InvokeRepeating invokes a method after an initial delay and then repeatedly at fixed intervals.
Describe how Unity scripting supports user interaction with input devices and how SDKs can extend device-specific input support.
Describe how to use Unity build settings to compile and deploy an XR system to a selected platform.
Explain why platform-specific SDKs are needed and outline the layered architecture and general steps for integrating an SDK into Unity.
Set up, configure, and deploy a Vuforia marker-based AR sample project on Android, including license, database, scene, player settings, and build steps.
Explain how the Vuforia sample project recognizes a target image and displays a 3D model, and how similar SDKs can extend Unity’s functionality.
Summarize the main points of the lecture and close the session.
